title: Dendrite geometry gave no clear gain in ramp-minus-step voltage threshold prediction in selected Allen mouse and human cells
abstract: We tested whether dendritic structure improves prediction of the voltage threshold difference between a slow current ramp and a one-second step. We linked Allen Cell Types reconstructions and electrical summaries by specimen ID. Ridge models used nested donor folds and passive physiology and cell labels as controls. In 495 mouse cells from 365 donors, added geometry reduced held-out mean squared error by 0.64%, with a conditional 95% donor interval from -2.28% to 3.50%. In 158 human cells from 35 donors, error reduction was -0.31%, with an interval from -6.52% to 5.92%. Thus neither primary test gave a clear gain. Intervals hold fitted predictions fixed. This is a protocol contrast in selected slice cells, not a test of a channel mechanism or intact-brain computation. Cut arbors, broad cell labels, source summary measurements, one fold partition, and clinical tissue limit inference. Code, source hashes, cell features, predictions, and checks are supplied.

display.caption: Protocol threshold contrasts and held-out prediction error changes. Positive MSE reduction favors geometry. Intervals resample donors while fitted predictions stay fixed.
